title: Diabetes Mellitus, Still Major Threat to Mortality from Various Causes

However, prediabetes comprises a wide range of dysglycemic and insulin-resistant subjects \[[10](#B10-dmj-43-273)]. Therefore, some previous studies about this issue that provides insights regarding how to divide prediabetic state into subgroups (impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance, or stage 1/2 impaired fasting glucose) showed inconsistent results \[[11](#B11-dmj-43-273)[12](#B12-dmj-43-273)]. For example, impaired fasting glucose stage 2 (110 to 125 mg/dL of fasting glucose), but not impaired fasting glucose stage 1 (100 to 109 mg/dL of fasting glucose), was significantly associated with higher all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality compared with normal glucose tolerance in a Korean study \[[13](#B13-dmj-43-273)]. Therefore, even though it was not the main focus of the study by Li et al. \[[5](#B5-dmj-43-273)], more extensive evidence on this topic will be needed later.[14](#B14-dmj-43-273)]. It was postulated that improvement in diabetes care including enhancement of medication adherence and management of cardiovascular risk factors might have contributed to lowering mortality in subjects with diabetes. Nonetheless, the mortality rate of people with diabetes is still about two-fold higher than those without diabetes. More advances in diabetes care and diabetes research are required to reduce mortality risk in patients with diabetes.
